transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what finally pushed me to come in is my concentration. It’s gotten unreliable. I’ll be reviewing a chart at the clinic, or even trying to lay out a watercolor wash, and then I realize I’ve read the same line three times because my mind’s gone off to everything that could go wrong.
Do you find that you worry a lot about different things, even when there’s no clear reason to worry?

Yes… I do. It sort of moves from one thing to another. I worry about whether my old patients are being looked after properly, whether the practice handoff was handled right financially… and, I suppose, whether I’ll be of any use once I’m fully retired. It feels like more than the situation really calls for.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or like you don’t have much energy lately?

Yes… more than I’d like to admit. By midafternoon I feel pretty worn out, and it doesn’t really seem to lift even if I’ve had a quiet morning or try to rest. Small things—like weeding a bit or standing at the easel—feel heavier than they should.
Have you been having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up earlier than you’d like?

Yes… most nights, I’d say. I’ll be tired when I get into bed, but once it’s quiet my mind starts going back over patient handoffs and money details. I do sleep some, but I’m often awake around four or five, feeling like I never really settled.
Have you been feeling like you're not worth much or that you're failing others, even when things are out of your control?
I don’t think so… not in that way. I get frustrated with myself, maybe, but I wouldn’t say I feel worthless.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, even if it's just a low-grade feeling?
I wouldn’t say depressed, no. Maybe a bit worn down some days, but not… down most of the day every day.
Have you found that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, like activities you once looked forward to such as painting or spending time with loved ones?
I… I don’t think so. I still enjoy things when I actually get to them. Maybe I’m a little less eager sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed a big change there.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless or fidgety without being able to settle down?
Not really… I haven’t noticed moving or talking slower. Maybe I get a bit keyed up at times, but I don’t know that it’s anything obvious.
Would you say that your mood has been consistently lower than usual, even if it's not severe, on most days over the past few weeks?
No… I don’t think it’s been consistently lower. I mean, I have off days, but not most days like that.
Have you been feeling guilty about things, even when you know logically that they aren't really your fault?
No… not really. I mean, I can second-guess myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I feel guilty over things that aren’t my fault.
Have you ever had sudden episodes where you felt intense fear or discomfort that came out of the blue, maybe with symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or feeling short of breath?
No… I don’t think I’ve had anything that sudden or out of the blue like that. I get uneasy sometimes, but not an episode with all those symptoms.
Do you find that your worrying is something you can’t seem to control, even when you try to stop thinking about these things?

Yeah… I suppose so. I try to talk myself down, you know, reason through it, like I would with a nervous patient. But then one thing turns into the next, and before I know it I’m checking emails again or going back over notes… asking the same question more than once. It’s hard to just let it go.
Would you say that your worrying and feeling keyed up or on edge happens on most days, and has been going on like this for several months?
Yes… most days, I’d say. It’s been going on since I started the formal retirement process—about a year and three months ago.
